Since you clicked…

A few proud moments.

If you’ve made it to this page, I’m taking that as permission to be a little proud. These awards mean a lot to me—and on a difficult research day, they’re a helpful nudge to keep going.

2025–2026

Wilson Bicentennial Graduate Fellowship

University of Virginia
Support for my doctoral research in laser processing and materials recovery.

A welcome vote of confidence for the next experiment.

2025

First place, Electrical Engineering poster

UVA Engineering Research Symposium
For work on laser-assisted silver recycling and AI-driven process automation.

Turns out the poster was worth all that rearranging.

2025

Second place, invited speaker presentation

UVA Engineering Research Symposium
Recognition for presenting my doctoral research.

A good reason to keep practicing the short explanation.

2025

UPLAMP travel award

Vilnius, Lithuania
Support to attend the summer school on ultra-short pulse laser applications in materials processing.

Learning about lasers came with a change of scenery.

2024

NSF-supported ANGEL-7 travel award

Charlottesville, Virginia
Support for the conference and tutorial on laser-generated nanoparticles.

More questions came home with me.

2019–2022

Institute Fellowship

IIT Delhi
Research fellowship support during my time in the Department of Physics.

Time and support to keep learning by doing.

2017–2019

Merit-cum-Means Scholarship

IIT Ropar
Scholarship support during my MSc in Physics.

An important step in a much longer journey.

2016

University Second Rank & Gold Medal in Computer Science

Rani Channamma University
Recognition during my BSc in Computer Science, Physics, and Mathematics.

An early milestone that still means a lot.

None of this happened alone. I’m grateful to the teachers, mentors, collaborators, and family who helped me get here.

Mahantesh Khetri

Charlottesville, Virginia.
Usually somewhere between a question and an experiment.
